Location : Lagos, Nigeria or Nairobi, Kenya.

About the role:
The PayG Phones TechOps Manager is accountable for the end-to-end technical operations of the PAYG Phones portfolio. The role ensures that MDM platforms, payment-triggered controls, security settings, partner integrations, and unlock operations remain stable, compliant, and scalable. This is an execution-focused role: it translates approved product, policy and commercial resolutions into steady operational delivery, while maintaining service continuity and control discipline across markets.
data.key_responsibilities:
1. MDM Platform Operations & Service Ownership 
  •  Act as the operational owner for all assisted PAYG Phones MDM environments: healthy configuration, access governance, tenant hygiene, and business continuity.  Administer device-control capabilities: enrollment, lock and unlock triggers, offline unlock paths, temporary unlocks, SIM controls, and lost-phone blocking, in line with approved product and policy rules. 
  • Define platform operating standards, monitoring thresholds, issue escalation paths, and rollback protocols for critical changes.  Implement and maintain approved MDM configurations consistently across markets; escalate design or policy gaps to Product and business owners. 
2.  Incident Management & Problem Resolution 
  • Run a structured incident management process for MDM, device-control, enrollment, unlock, SMS, and integration failures. 
  •  Prioritize incidents by business severity, restore service rapidly, communicate impact clearly, and coordinate fixes with Engineering, vendors, and Operations. 
  •  Maintain an issue tracker with ownership, ETA, status confidence, escalation level, and preventive-action follow-through. 
  •  Guide post-incident root cause evaluation; ensure corrective and preventive actions are implemented and verified.
3.  Unlock Operations & Customer Control Journeys 
  •  Own operational execution and reliability for online unlocks, offline unlocks, USSD-based unlock flows, temporary unlocks, and post-payment device release processes. 
  • Monitor unlock success rates and investigate failure patterns by market, OEM, MDM, app version, and integration point. 
  • Maintain resilient fallback procedures for high-risk customer-impact scenarios while minimizing fraud and policy leakage. 
  •  Partner with Collections, Customer Care, and Field Operations so operational teams comprehend approved unlock pathways, exception handling, and approval controls. 
4. Security, Risk & Compliance Controls 
  • Maintain strong control over MDM security updates, license lifecycle, access rights, and configuration changes across all assisted platforms. 
  •  Own risk dashboards, compliance checks, and control reviews that surface service exposure, misconfiguration, aging licenses, or policy breaches before they create customer or revenue risk. 
  •  Coordinate blocking controls for lost phones, misuse scenarios, and high-risk device exceptions at server, tenant, or MDM level as applicable. 
  •  Assist internal audit, compliance, and InfoSec requests with evidence, process documentation, and remediation tracking. 
5.  Vendor, Partner & Integration Management 
  •  Serve as the primary technical operations counterpart to OEMs, MDM vendors and integration providers. 
  •  Track vendor performance against uptime, defect resolution, roadmap dedication, security fixes, and launch deliverables.  Escalate unresolved partner issues with clear evidence, business impact articulation, and proposed mitigation options. 
6. Project Delivery & Change Implementation 
  •  Coordinate TechOps workstreams from related Phone projects and deliverables: migrations, unlock operationalization, security update optimization, launch enablement, reporting improvements, and process redesign. 
  • Break initiatives into milestones, reliance, owners, risks, and test-readiness criteria.. 
  •  Balance project delivery with day-to-day operational escalations through a transparent prioritization framework. 
7. Data, Reporting & resolution 
  • Own reporting requirements for device operations, incidents, unlock performance, risk signals, license status, and open-issue backlog. 
  • Develop or validate operational dashboards and data pipelines used for service visibility and market-level conclusion (Looker or equivalent). 
  • Use data to identify recurring failure patterns, process bottlenecks, control weaknesses, and opportunities for automation. 
  •  Provide concise operational reviews to senior stakeholders: trend breakdown, risk commentary, service-impact summaries, and resolution requests. 
 8. Process Governance & Documentation 
  • Create and maintain SOPs, FAQs, control frameworks, troubleshooting guides, approval matrices, and escalation maps for all major TechOps processes. 
  •  Standardize repeatable workflows: issue logging, incident reviews, unlock approvals, license monitoring, and launch checklists. 
  •  Keep documentation usable by frontline, country, and assist teams: not only technical specialists. 
  •  Embed lessons learned from incidents and projects into documented operating practice. 
9. Cross-Functional Management
  • Coordinate effectively across Product, Engineering, Commercial, Customer Operations, Risk, Compliance, Collections, Finance, and Country teams. 
  •  Translate technical constraints into business language, and business priorities into executable technical actions. 
  •  Influence prioritization, build consensus during incidents or launches, and keep stakeholders aligned on trade-offs and timelines. 
  •  Coach evaluators or coordinators assist TechOps processes and raise overall operating maturity. 
10. Field Immersion & Ground Truth 
  • Spend regular time in-country with agents, PayG customers, service desks and country teams. Ride along on device activations, unlock scenarios, payment collections and post-payment device releases so you see MDM, unlock flows and integrations behave in the real world — not just in dashboards. 
  •  Use every field visit to surface pain points, edge cases and workarounds that don't show up in the ticketing system. Convert them into concrete follow-ups: an SOP update, a configuration hardening, a test case, a UAT scenario, a vendor escalation, or a training request via the Training Liaison. 
  •  Never be an armchair TechOps manager. Field reality drives the PayG Phones TechOps backlog.
data.key_responsibilities_header: What you will be expected to do
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
• Bachelor's degree or its equivalent in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Telecommunications, or a related technical field. 
  •  Minimum of 5 years of experience in Technology Operations, Product Operations, IT Operations, or Enterprise Mobility. 
  •  4+ years managing production technology platforms, including Incident, Problem, Release, and Change Management. 
  •  4+ years of people management and managing cross-functional technical teams. 
  •  4+ years of Mobile Device Management (MDM) experience (e.g., Samsung Knox, Android Enterprise, NuovoPay, Intune, Workspace ONE). 
  •  Experience assisting multi-country/global operations. 
  • Strong experience in vendor management, including SLA governance and technical escalations. 
  •  Hands-on knowledge of Android ecosystem, APIs, SQL, system integrations, and data evaluation. 
  •  Proven experience delivering large-scale technology rollouts and managing production environments.

Job Location:  Nairobi, Kenya or Lagos, Nigeria


About the role:
The Senior Product Designer (UX Designer), based in Nairobi or Lagos. You will report to the Head of Product, Enterprise Products.

You will own the experience of the products our customers, field agents and our staff teams use every day. That covers the apps our Energy Officers use to sell, onboard and service customers. It also covers the products our customers use to buy, pay for and manage their energy. It covers the tools our staff uses to manage the inventory, sales, collections, incentives, etc every day.  And it covers the design system that holds all of it.

The people you design for are not like you. Many are first-time smartphone users. They work outdoors, on low-end Android devices, on patchy networks, often in their second or third language. A design succeeds here when an agent can close a sale in a village at the end of a long day. It is not judged by how the screen looks in a portfolio.

We also want an AI-first approach to design. You reach for AI to explore concepts, generate variants and pressure-test copy. You prototype before writing a specification. You ask “can AI do this better” first, not as an afterthought.

This role covers design end to end. Research, flows, interaction design, visual design, prototyping and handoff. We expect all of it done the AI-first way: faster, sharper, and built to scale.
data.key_responsibilities:
1. Research with the people who actually use our products
  • Spend time in the field with Energy Officers, customers and operations teams. Watch them work. Do not rely on second-hand reports.
  • Run usability tests, contextual interviews and concept tests in market.
  • Turn what you learn into choice the team acts on, not decks that get filed away.
2. Flows and interaction design
  • Design the end-to-end journeys behind sales, onboarding, collections, servicing and assist.
  • Map the offline steps as well as the on-screen ones. Most of our journeys start on paper or in conversation.
  • Simplify flows that have grown complicated over years of feature additions.
3. Visual design and craft
  • Take work from rough concept to production-ready screens.
  • Hold a high bar on typography, spacing, ranking and legibility in bright sunlight on small screens.
  • Make the interface teachable. A new agent should be productive on day one.
4. Design for real constraints
  • Design for low-end Android devices, small screens and limited storage.
  • Design for intermittent flow. Offline states, sync and failure recovery are part of the design, not an engineering afterthought.
  • Design for low digital literacy and for multiple languages. Assume text will be longer once translated.
5. The design system
  • Own our collective component library and design standards.
  • Keep it in step with what engineering actually ships. A system nobody uses is worse than none.
  • Document patterns so other designers and engineers can apply them without asking you.
6. Prototype before spec
  • Build clickable prototypes to answer open questions early.
  • Use AI tools to generate variants, draft copy and explore directions quickly.
  • Put prototypes in front of real users and change your mind when they tell you to.
7. Handoff and working with engineering
  • Produce handoff-ready files, specs and states that engineers can build from without guesswork.
  • Cover the unglamorous cases: empty states, errors, loading, long names, missing data, poor network.
  • Review builds before release and hold the bar on implementation quality.
8. Measure whether the design worked
  • Define what success looks like before the design ships: task completion, time on task, error and drop-off rates.
  • Work with product and data teams to read adoption and funnel data after release.
  • Go back and fix what the data says is not working.
9. Team Work
  • Work closely with product managers, engineers and market operations teams through the full product lifecycle.
  • Bring evidence to design debates. Be willing to be overruled, and be willing to argue your case.
  • Keep stakeholders informed at every stage.
10. Travel
  • Travel as required to Sun King markets, including Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Tanzania and Myanmar, with regular field visits to agents and customers.
data.key_responsibilities_header: What you would be expected to do:
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
1.      Background and approach
  • A portfolio of shipped product work (mandatory). We want two or three cases in depth: the problem, what you tried, what you did, and what happened after launch.
  • 5–7 years designing digital products, with meaningful time on mobile.
  • Experience designing for users who are not like you, ideally in emerging markets, field operations, fintech or last-mile distribution.
  • Able to structure and evaluate ambiguous problems.
  • Clear communication in writing. You will explain design choice to people who are not designers.
  • A proactive attitude and willingness to get hands-on. We are small and you will do your own research, design and testing.
  • A formal design degree is welcome but not required. The portfolio matters more.
2.      Language
  • Professional working proficiency in English (mandatory). You will work with colleagues and stakeholders across our markets in Africa and Asia.
  • A local market language such as Swahili, French, Hausa, Yoruba or Luganda is a strong plus for field research.
3.    Essential skills  
  • Expert in Figma, including components, variables, auto layout and prototyping.
  • Hands-on experience building or maintaining a design system.
  • Practical research skills: usability testing, contextual inquiry and field interviews, run by you rather than outsourced.
  • Android design conventions and Material Design, applied with judgement rather than by default.
  • Accessibility and legibility fundamentals: contrast, touch targets, text scaling, and patterns that work for low-literacy users.
  • Enough data literacy to read a funnel, an adoption chart or an A/B test result and act on it.
  • Comfortable using AI tools in your design workflow, for concepts, copy, research synthesis and prototypes.
4.    Good to have
  • Experience designing offline-first or intermittently integrated applications.
  • Front-end familiarity (HTML, CSS, or React) — enough to talk to engineers about what is expensive to build.
  • Motion design or illustration.
  • Service design experience covering journeys that cross online and offline steps.
  • Exposure to pay-as-you-go, asset finance, microfinance or emerging-market lending.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL.

Job Location: Afikpo, Ebonyi State

About the role:
The Area Business Manager will coordinate sales, collections and distribution operations in the area they are assigned for the direct distribution of Sun King Solar products sold on Pay-As-You-Basis (also called and recognized as “EasyBuy” Business unit) through a network of agents called as “Energy Officer”.  The Area Business Manager is ultimately accountable for generating sales, ensuring collections are timely and accurate and keeping the entire Direct Distribution growing rapidly in a sustainable manager.
data.key_responsibilities:
• Hire & retain Energy Officers: Hire, train and maintain a team of at least 40  Sun King Energy Officers in the area. Use multiple avenues for finding the right talent to sell Sun King EasyBuy products with the help of village influencers such as the village heads, teachers, religious heads, doctors, farmers and others, as applicable. Create a reputation and goodwill for the mission of Sun King to provide clean, affordable and reliable source of energy in their areas.
  • Training of Energy Officers: Provide training to the Energy Officers on several aspects of the business such as sales, collections, product, technical, inventory and logistics related. Ensure that they are fully supervised in the best professional manner demonstrating highest levels of integrity, ethics and professionalism while dealing with customers.
  • Provide role clarity to Energy Officers: Provide complete clarity to Energy Officers related to their day to day tasks, sales & collections plans, routes and targets. This includes, ensuring Energy Officers have sales route/area to sell in, they know on how to demonstrate and sell Sun King products, they have the confidence to be able to present and resolve basic customer queries on the spot and they have access to Area Business Manager at all times in case of questions and concerns.
  • Daily field visits: Have a weekly touchpoint with every Energy Officer in your area – either through in-person meetings, making a sale to the customer in your area or having a call. Resolve all possible issues faced by the Energy Officers and report them to your Regional Business Manager, every week. Ensure that first 5 sales of each Energy Officer is done along with the Area Business Manager in the area, by each Energy Officer to ensure that the core sales and collection process is fully understood by each Energy Officer.
  • Work with Energy Officers: Conduct joint field work with a group of Energy Officers to provide sales and collection training on a weekly basis and drive EO engagement. This includes doing night activations, market activations, visiting local communities and gatherings such as SACCOs, Self Help groups, retail centers and markets to make group sales.
  • Exceed your sales & collections targets: Meet or exceed sales and collection targets established on 2nd of every month by your Regional Business Manager. Provide daily, weekly updates on sales, EO recruitments, Customer issues and resolutions, in alignment with your Regional Business Manager.
  • Drive robust field sales processes: Review collection progress with your Energy Officers daily and provide adequate training to them on driving better collections in your areas. This includes, customer and area profiling, ensuring regular and timely collection follow-ups, resolving customer issues to ensure they make payments and ultimately repossessing the systems as a last recourse in case the customer defaults.
  • Remain externally focused: Keep an eye on companies selling similar products within your area and ensure you take adequate measures to protect and grow our business from pressures. Pre-inform your management team and take measures to ensure Sun King remains a paramount brand name in Solar products for your area.
  • Resolve customer issues: Provide world-class customer service to your customers as it relates to product delivery, training on how to use and make payments, installation, after sales warranty issues. Ensure that you work with your Energy Officers to establish clear expectations and processes to resolve all customer issues within 24 hours.
  • Control Marketing & Other  spend: Provide adequate marketing materials & equipment (such as smartphones) necessary to all your Energy Officers. Ensure we get maximum return on investment for all the costs we incur in areas of marketing, supply chain, store maintenance and smartphone issuance.
  • Review meetings with Energy Officers: Conduct weekly table meetings with Energy Officers and ensure that you have RBM present in those meetings to resolve any outstanding customers or EO issues. Coordinate, plan and organize the meeting to have maximum attendance and progress. Recognize outstanding performers from time to time and ensure the motivation of Energy Officers is maintained at an all-time high.
  • Grow Retail presence: Ensure the retail network in your Area grows with the help of the Cluster leaders, hired under you.

Job Location: Nairobi, Kenya

About the Role

The Credit Manager - PayGo Phones Kenya is a field-based position within the Global Risk and Credit team. The role focuses on overseeing credit and related risk areas within the PAYGo business in Kenya. It involves shaping, implementing, and maintaining effective credit risk controls and operational practices to strengthen portfolio quality and regulatory adherence.
data.key_responsibilities:
Portfolio Performance Oversight
  • Review portfolio performance to identify customers showing early signs of repayment difficulties through data review and direct field engagement.
  • Track portfolio risk indicators and ensure timely escalation and visibility.
  • Produce consistent and accurate portfolio performance and risk indicator reports.
  • Monitor regional, area, and product-level trends and recommend corrective actions to address emerging risk exposures.
Audit & Compliance
  • Carry out internal reviews to identify gaps across credit-related processes, including underwriting, collections, onboarding, repossession, and customer detail updates.
  • Confirm alignment with internal policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Document findings clearly and outline practical risk mitigation actions.
Collections & Field Interventions
  • Apply preventative collection approaches, including KYC and onboarding practices that enhance customer quality.
  • Design and roll out field-informed collection approaches in partnership with field teams to improve recovery outcomes.
  • Evaluate existing policies and their portfolio impact, proposing updates informed by market conditions and field insights.
  • Improve portfolio segmentation by aligning customer buckets with appropriate ownership models and recommending adjustments where required.
Pilot & Initiative Management
  • Oversee field pilots to ensure they are tracked, documented, and measured against defined success criteria through engagement with relevant teams.
Fraud Case Oversight
  • Ensure reported fraud cases are reviewed promptly and resolved within established timelines.
Reporting & Documentation
  • Compile structured field reports covering data summaries, operational observations, and process documentation.
  • Maintain consistency and accuracy in risk and portfolio performance reporting.
  • Conduct market and sector research and translate findings into recommendations that strengthen Sun King’s market position across sales and collections.
data.key_responsibilities_header: What you will be expected to do:
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Risk Management, or a related business discipline.
  • 10+ years of relevant experience within credit, risk, audit, or data-focused functions, including at least 5 years in a people or operational oversight capacity.
  • Professional certification in Credit Management, Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field is an advantage.
  • Practical exposure to data gathering and field-based assessments.
  • Strong planning, organisation, and attention to detail.
  • High adaptability, flexibility, and comfort operating in dynamic environments.
  • Structured problem-solving approach with the ability to translate complex issues into practical actions.
  • Ability to guide teams and influence operational improvements through clarity and direction.
  • Clear and assured written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work constructively across teams.
  • Willingness to spend approximately 70% of time in the field.
  • Demonstrates discretion, ethical judgment, and appropriate handling of restricted information.
